reasons: Only 1 of 10 sections was provided, so most test logic could not be reviewed.
Tests were not run while writing these notes.

terms.meaning: a set of rules that sorts items into categories
a stage of the project, such as design or construction
whether an item matters for the physical model
the tree of project work packages, often shortened to WBS
quality assurance, checks that work meets requirements
the 3D shape of an item in the model
a schedule task cleaned into a standard form

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for schedule scope tests
sections.what: Brings in the classifier, the location helper, and the activity and phase types the tests use.
sections.why: Likely reason: each test feeds a schedule task through the classifier and location code.
sections.watch_out: Renaming any of these helpers breaks every test in this file.

sections.name: activity
sections.title: Sample activity builder and admin name list
sections.what: Builds a sample schedule activity inside a test project with a fixed construction location, then supplies a list of administrative activity names such as bid awards, conceptual plans and stakeholder mailers. The tests use these to check how the app classifies each name.
sections.why: Gives every classification test the same realistic input, so only the activity name or WBS path changes between tests.
sections.watch_out: The names in this list are examples from real schedules, so removing one removes its coverage without any warning.

sections.name: test_administrative_work_does_not_acquire_geometry_from_construction_wbs
sections.title: Paperwork activities stay out of the 3D model
sections.what: Checks that administrative activities, such as bids, awards, QA panel work and mailers, are classified as abstract rather than physical, and that the classification evidence mentions the administrative rule.
sections.why: Likely reason: paperwork has no physical shape, so it should not be drawn as a building part in the 3D view.
sections.watch_out: The app recognizes these items by name patterns, so a new paperwork name that does not match a rule will be drawn as physical work.

sections.name: test_actual_physical_work_stays_physical
sections.title: Real construction work stays physical
sections.what: Checks that genuine construction activities such as grading, foundations, control house installation, equipment installation and field wiring are classified as physical.
sections.why: Ensures real construction is not accidentally dropped from the 3D model by the administrative rules.
sections.watch_out: A rule that is too broad could hide real work, so this list should grow when new construction names appear.

sections.name: test_shop_wiring_is_narratable_offsite_not_an_onsite_object
sections.title: Shop wiring is offsite, building work is onsite
sections.what: Checks that shop wiring is treated as physical but offsite, while constructing a shop building is treated as onsite.
sections.why: Likely reason: wiring made in a shop is not installed at the site yet, so it should be shown as narrated offsite work rather than an onsite object.
sections.watch_out: The word shop decides location here, so a name that mentions a shop for another reason can be placed offsite by mistake.

sections.name: test_grading_does_not_inherit_procurement_phase_from_contract_services_wbs
sections.title: Grading keeps its excavation phase
sections.what: Checks that a grading activity under a Contract Services WBS path is still assigned the excavation phase, not the procurement phase.
sections.why: Likely reason: the activity name should decide the construction phase, not the parent folder that holds the contract work.
sections.watch_out: If the WBS path rules are changed to take precedence over the name, grading will move to the wrong phase.

sections.name: test_qa_asset_installation_is_not_the_same_as_performing_qa
sections.title: Installing a QA building is not doing QA
sections.what: Checks that installing a quality assurance lab building is physical work, while a quality assurance panel activity is abstract paperwork.
sections.why: Likely reason: the words quality assurance appear in both physical and paperwork activities, so the test separates the two cases.
sections.watch_out: Matching on the words quality assurance alone would mix these two categories, so the rule must check the rest of the name.

sections.name: test_explicit_onsite_installation_overrides_shop_noun
sections.title: Explicit onsite installation beats shop wording
sections.what: Checks that installing shop wiring on site is treated as onsite, while shop wiring that is only for installation on site is treated as offsite.
sections.why: Likely reason: the verb install with an onsite phrase should decide the location, and the shop wording alone should not.
sections.watch_out: The two phrases differ only in word order, so small wording changes can flip the location result.

sections.name: test_preconstruction_work_never_builds_geometry
sections.title: Preconstruction work never creates geometry
sections.what: Checks that design, bid, staking, vendor drawing, land and publication activities under preconstruction WBS paths are all classified as abstract and create no 3D shape.
sections.why: Likely reason: preconstruction tasks happen before anything is built, so showing them as objects would mislead the viewer.
sections.watch_out: The test relies on the WBS path as well as the name, so moving these activities to a different folder can change the result.

sections.name: test_contractor_work_under_contract_services_stays_physical
sections.title: Contractor work under contract services stays physical
sections.what: Checks that construction names under a Contract Services WBS path, such as foundation crew support, remain physical.
sections.why: Likely reason: contractor field work is real construction even though its folder is labeled contract services.
sections.watch_out: A rule that treats every Contract Services item as paperwork would break this test and hide real work.

summary: Tests the rules that decide whether a schedule task, such as paperwork, procurement, inspection or on-site work, should appear as a physical object in the 3D site, and in which project phase.
purpose: Makes sure administrative and planning tasks never create geometry, and that real physical work does.
why: Likely reason: schedules mix physical work with paperwork and procurement, so the model must not draw the paperwork. Reason not stated in the code beyond the test names.
how: Based on the imports and test names, each test builds a schedule task and checks the phase, materiality and object type it receives. The test bodies were not in the packet, so these details are inferred from names.
inputs: Sample schedule task names, optional work breakdown paths, and location context.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest.
risks: Only the setup section was provided, so the classification cases could not be fully reviewed.
debug: Check the failing test name, then the phase and materiality rules in the classifier module.
